title: Brand-aware dark-mode token mapping and component overrides for console charts & tables
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Brand themes currently map poorly into deep-dark console skins. Charts lose hierarchy (accent series flatten), table row separators and focus rings have insufficient contrast, and a handful of button variants end up with visual artifacts when elevation tokens are inverted. This ticket defines a brand-aware token mapping approach and a set of component overrides for charts, tables, and key buttons to ensure consistent hierarchy, accessibility, and predictable brand accents across light/dark/brand themes.

Goals:
- Create a deterministic token transform for converting semantic light tokens into dark tokens for both neutral and brand themes.
- Provide component-level override rules where token transforms produce poor results (charts color scales, table dividers, skeletons).
- Ensure all adjusted tokens meet AA contrast for primary interactive elements and organized guidance for custom brand colors.
- Deliver a migration guide and canary rollout plan for console-2026.03.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Semantic-first tokens: define the full set of semantic tokens to cover surfaces, elevation layers, interactive states, text/labels, and chart scales (e.g. surface-0..4, interactive-primary, text-muted, chart-accent-1..6).
2) Color-transform pipeline: implement a transform function in the design system that converts semantic light tokens to dark counterparts using perceptual adjustments (Lab-based delta, preserve relative luminance hierarchy, clamp saturation for brand accents). This avoids hard-coding per-brand dark palettes.
3) Brand-aware exceptions: introduce a small exceptions map where the transform is overridden for a brand color if the computed result fails contrast or hue preservation checks. Exceptions live in theme config and are minimal by default.
4) Component overrides: charts and tables get targeted overrides:
   - Charts: provide an algorithmic palette generator that derives series colors from the brand accent but enforces minimum contrast with chart background and between series (use contrast-aware desaturation and alternation). Include a fallback neutral palette for heavy multi-series charts.
   - Tables: adjust row-hover, zebra, divider tokens to maintain separation in deep dark; move from 1px hairline to 1.5px where necessary and use softened highlight color for focus rings.
   - Buttons: expose an elevation blending layer that prevents rim artifacts when surface tokens invert in dark mode (use subtle alpha overlays rather than pure color flips).
5) Tooling & testing: add visual snapshots (Percy/Chromatic) for brand variants, automated contrast checks in the token pipeline, and an accessibility checklist for manual QA.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list):
- Token transform implemented and documented in design system repo.
- Charts and tables show no regression across 4 brand themes in visual diffs.
- Contrast check automated tests pass for primary interactive states.
- Migration guide and rollout plan sign-off from Eng + PM.

Migration & rollout notes:
- Phase 1: internal canary (10% of console traffic) with new tokens applied to a subset of orgs.
- Phase 2: expand to all non-enterprise orgs after 1 week of telemetry review.
- Enterprise opt-in for private deployments (document config knobs for brand exception mapping).

Risks: potential visual regressions for custom brand palettes; will mitigate via exceptions map and explicit design review for top-20 customers.

References: Figma spec and component examples, token mapping draft in Confluence, related engineering tickets.

acceptance_criteria: Token transform function added to design-system with examples for neutral + 3 brand themes.
Charts render with preserved series hierarchy across all supported themes (visual tests green).
Tables show readable dividers and focus states in deep-dark (AA for text on interactive backgrounds).
Design doc + migration guide published and signed off by ENG and PM.
Automated contrast checks integrated into CI for token pipeline.
notes: Trade-off: algorithmic transforms increase predictability for unknown brands but may still need per-brand tuning for marketing-heavy palettes.
Decision: prefer subtle alpha overlays for elevation fixes over hard color inversion to reduce flicker during theme transitions.
Follow-up: schedule design reviews with top 10 paying customers for brand exception opt-in before GA rollout.
